decisions.reason: As a recently launched extension of the core coolant-management business that has already been publicly presented, it fits the firm's strategy and is unlikely to be withdrawn so soon without clear failure evidence.

This centrifuge builds directly on established process-media capabilities, likely required meaningful engineering investment, and a large German machinery firm would usually continue backing it after launch.

Although coolant nozzles may involve lower sunk investment than larger systems, they still complement the existing offer and there is no sign of persistent market disappointment that would justify an early exit.
The scraper belt chip conveyor is close to the firm's established conveying portfolio, and with public market introduction and normal industrial sales cycles management would likely persist with it.
The magnetic belt chip conveyor sits squarely within the firm's known product family, so sunk development effort and product-line coherence make withdrawal within a year unlikely.
As another close-to-core chip conveyor variant, it supports a broad catalogue strategy and escalation of commitment makes management more likely to retain it absent strong contrary results.
